To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Rational Terms R2 of the 1-loop QCD amplitude, which are the terms that are not proportional to the tree-level amplitude, can be written in terms of a set of Feynmann rules that are independent of the number of external legs, provided the number of external lines is not larger than the number of propagators.

we have derived a complete set of Feyman rules for the R2 terms of the QCD one loop amplitude, which are valid for processes with any number of external legs, and which are expressed in both the 't Hoot Veltman and the four dimensional helicity schemes, and in terms of both color configurations and color connection language.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the Rational Terms of the 1-loop QCD amplitudes.
a systematic study of the Rational Terms of QCD at the 1-loop level, with particular attention to the R2 terms, that are the most difficult to compute.
the calculation of the Rational Terms of the QCD amplitudes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Feynman rules for the R2 terms are now known for any QCD 4-point 1-loop amplitude, and can be easily extended to any number of external legs.
, for any 1-loop calculation, the R2 part of the amplitude is fully determined by the knowledge of the 2- and 3-point vertices and of the 1-loop propagators.
the R2 contribution is completely described by the Feynman Rules given in this paper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided the full list of Feynman rules to compute the R2 terms in the QCD 2-point, 3-point and 4-point functions in the 't Hooft Veltmanscheme and in the Four-Dimensional Helicity scheme, and we have shown that these rules are complete.

the R2 terms are completely described by a finite number of Feynman rules, and that they can be computed by means of the standard Feynman diagrams, with no need to introduce new diagrams or new vertices.

, given a generic QCD 1- loop process, the Rational Terms are completely determined by the tree level amplitude, by the number and type of external legs, and by the choice of the regularization scheme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Rational Terms can be computed in a fully automatic way, without the need to resort to any special technique.
the Feynman Rules for the R2 part of the 1-loop amputated amplitudes are very simple and compact.
the R2 contribution is fully determined by the R1 one.
